summary: GRN 908 is a resubmission (replacing GRN 866) covering a lipase enzyme preparation derived from a self-cloned GM strain of Penicillium camemberti (AE-LGS) for use as a processing aid in dairy processing and fats/oils processing. The notice relies heavily on GRN 68 (non-GM strain, AE-LG) by incorporation by reference under 21 C.F.R. § 170.215, with the pivotal safety study (Kondo et al. 1994, 90-day rat gavage) drawn from that prior notice. The notice provides a structured equivalence bridge between AE-LGS and AE-LG through SDS-PAGE, biochemical characterization, and TOS/activity comparisons. FDA raised nine questions during review, all of which were addressed in supplemental responses (December 2020 and January 2021), including clarification of DNA integration confirmation, genetic stability, manufacturing process details, allergen controls, and exposure methodology. The notice is substantively complete; residual issues are primarily documentation and adequacy concerns around the manufacturing description (resolved in part through Q&A), the publication status of the pivotal Kondo et al. study, and the breadth of the test-article bridge given the higher-purity GM product. No critical evidentiary gaps are identified. The notice was closed with a 'no questions' response from FDA in February 2021.

findings.title: Publication status of pivotal 90-day toxicity study (Kondo et al. 1994) requires verification
findings.summary: The notice identifies Kondo et al. (1994) as the pivotal safety data for the GRAS determination. The study is cited as a journal article (Food Chem Toxic 32(8):685-696) and was originally submitted to FDA in GRN 68. The notice does not explicitly confirm that the published journal article is publicly available and peer-reviewed in the current submission; it is referenced as incorporated from GRN 68. The journal Food and Chemical Toxicology is a peer-reviewed publication, but the notice itself does not state this, and the study was conducted on the non-GM test article (LGK, Lipase G Amano 50) rather than the GM product (Lipase GS Amano 250G). The pivotal role of this study and its public peer-reviewed status are not affirmatively stated in GRN 908.
findings.recommendedAction: Confirm in the notice body that Kondo et al. (1994) is a publicly available, peer-reviewed publication and that the notifier independently concludes safety based on its data rather than relying on GRN 68's outcome.

findings.title: Manufacturing process description relies on GRN 68 incorporation without full in-notice summary
findings.summary: Section 2.2 of GRN 908 states that 'A detailed description of the manufacturing process, which was provided in GRN 68 and is incorporated herein, reflects the current process with the exception of minor changes made to improve process efficiency.' The actual manufacturing steps are not described in GRN 908 itself. FDA raised this as Question 6 during review, and a detailed process summary was provided in the December 3, 2020 response letter. However, this information was not incorporated into the notice body itself, leaving the notice as filed incomplete with respect to manufacturing description. The response letter clarifies fermentation conditions, filtration sequence, heat treatment, pH adjustment, ethanol precipitation, and diluent identity (maltodextrin, not dextrin as stated in the notice).
findings.recommendedAction: Incorporate the manufacturing process summary provided in the December 2020 Q&A response directly into the notice body (Section 2.2) to make the notice self-contained, and correct the diluent identification from dextrin to maltodextrin.

findings.title: Higher specific activity of GM-strain product relative to 90-day toxicity test article not fully bridged at the exposure level
findings.summary: Table 2 shows that the GM-strain product (LGS-Y69-001) has an activity of 913,000 Units/g (986.2 Units/mg TOS), approximately 3.5-fold higher than the mean of the non-GM batches (279.9 Units/mg TOS) and approximately 7.5-fold higher than the test article (LGK-000602, 132.3 Units/mg TOS). The notice states the lipase from AE-LGS is 'of a higher purity than that derived from non-GM strains as indicated by activity (U/g) assays' and that the products are 'equivalent,' but does not explicitly address whether the higher specific activity of the GM product at the same TOS-based use levels results in meaningfully higher enzymatic exposure in food. The EDI is calculated on a TOS basis, which may understate functional enzyme exposure if the GM product is substantially more active per unit TOS.
findings.recommendedAction: Provide an explicit analysis of whether the higher specific activity of the GM-strain product at the same TOS-based use levels results in any meaningful difference in functional enzyme exposure compared to the test article, or confirm that TOS-based dosing in the 90-day study is the appropriate metric for safety bridging.

findings.title: Incorporation of GRN 68 is properly identified but independent conclusion could be more explicitly stated
findings.summary: The notice incorporates GRN 68 by reference under 21 C.F.R. § 170.215, identifies the underlying information (manufacturing process, pathogenicity study, mycotoxin screening, pivotal toxicity study), and explains its role. The notice states its own GRAS conclusion for the GM-strain product. However, the narrative in Part 6.2 closely tracks GRN 68's safety analysis and the notice does not explicitly state that its GRAS conclusion is independent of GRN 68's outcome (i.e., the 2001 'no questions' letter). The cover letter notes 'No additional information is provided in the enclosed GRAS notice as compared to GRN 866,' which could be read as relying on the prior review outcome rather than independently evaluating the evidence.
findings.recommendedAction: Add an explicit statement in the narrative that the GRAS conclusion for the GM-strain product is based on independent evaluation of the incorporated and new evidence, and is not contingent on the outcome of GRN 68.

findings.title: CPA production potential of AE-LGS strain not directly characterized; reliance on non-detection in finished product
findings.summary: The notice acknowledges that CPA is a mycotoxin of potential concern for some P. camemberti strains and that no published data exist regarding CPA production by P. camemberti U-150 (AE-LG). CPA was not detected in the enzyme preparations from AE-LG (per GRN 68) or AE-LGS (per Figure 4 mycotoxin screening). However, the notice does not characterize whether AE-LGS has been tested for CPA production capacity under fermentation conditions, relying solely on non-detection in the finished product. Ostry et al. (2018) is cited as calling for further chronic toxicity and carcinogenicity studies for CPA, which the notice acknowledges but does not resolve.
findings.recommendedAction: Clarify whether AE-LGS has been assessed for CPA production potential under fermentation conditions, or confirm that finished-product non-detection at the stated LOD is the appropriate and sufficient control measure, with reference to the LOD relative to any applicable threshold.

safetySignals.label: Cyclopiazonic acid (CPA) production potential by P. camemberti
safetySignals.summary: The notice acknowledges that CPA is a mycotoxin of potential concern for some P. camemberti strains under certain environmental conditions, citing Le Bars (1979) and Císarová et al. (2012). No published data exist on CPA production by P. camemberti U-150 (AE-LG). CPA was not detected in finished enzyme preparations from either AE-LG or AE-LGS at the stated LODs. Ostry et al. (2018) calls for further chronic toxicity and carcinogenicity studies. The signal is mitigated by non-detection in finished product but the absence of strain-specific production data and the acknowledged need for further chronic toxicity data warrant monitoring.
evidence: Le Bars (1979): 20 P. camemberti strains all produced CPA
Císarová et al. (2012): 12 of 14 P. camemberti strains produced CPA
CPA not detected in AE-LGS enzyme preparation at <7.5 μg/kg LOD
Ostry et al. (2018): further chronic toxicity studies warranted for CPA

citations.excerpt: Le Bars (1979) reported that each of 20 strains of P. camemberti isolated from cheese produced CPA at levels greatly dependent on the strain and environmental parameters (medium, temperature, and incubation time).

citations.excerpt: Based on an exhaustive review of the published research on CPA, Ostry et al. (2018) concluded: CPA is a potentially serious mycotoxin and its toxicity to several animal species warrant further chronic toxicity and carcinogenicity studies.

safetySignals.label: Occupational allergenicity to P. camemberti by inhalation
safetySignals.summary: Two published case reports (Marchisio et al. 1999; Merget et al. 2008) document occupational allergic reactions (extrinsic allergic alveolitis, IgE-mediated asthma) in workers with repeated inhalation exposure to P. camemberti in food manufacturing settings. The notice addresses this signal by distinguishing the route of exposure (inhalation of high levels of the organism vs. dietary exposure to a purified extracellular enzyme preparation not containing the production organism) and concludes no dietary safety concern. The distinction is scientifically supported and the signal is resolved for the intended use.
evidence: Marchisio et al. (1999): possible extrinsic allergic alveolitis by inhalation in salami factory worker
Merget et al. (2008): IgE-mediated asthma in dry-sausage packer with P. camemberti exposure
Notice distinguishes inhalation occupational exposure from dietary exposure to purified enzyme

citations.excerpt: The circumstances and route of exposure for the reported cases of allergic reactions in workers after repeated contact with high levels of P. camemberti used in finishing dried sausages do not raise safety concerns for dietary exposure to low levels of an extracellular lipase enzyme preparation derived P. camemberti and not containing the production organism.
citations.section: Part 6.1 Safety of Penicillium camemberti AE-LGS

safetySignals.label: Higher specific activity of GM-strain product relative to toxicity test article
safetySignals.summary: The GM-strain product (AE-LGS) has a specific activity approximately 7.5-fold higher per mg TOS than the test article used in the 90-day rat study (LGK). The notice calculates the EDI and NOAEL on a TOS basis, which may not fully capture functional enzyme exposure differences. The notice does not explicitly address whether the higher specific activity at the same TOS-based use levels results in meaningfully different biological activity in food. The 399-fold safety margin provides substantial buffer, but the basis for TOS-equivalence as the appropriate metric for safety bridging is not explicitly justified.
evidence: Table 2: GM product 986.2 Units/mg TOS vs. test article 132.3 Units/mg TOS (7.5-fold difference)
EDI calculated on TOS basis (3.8 mg TOS/kg bw/day)
NOAEL expressed as 1515 mg TOS/kg bw (399-fold margin)
Notice states products are 'equivalent' without addressing activity-based exposure
